taoism.title: Zhuangzi
taoism.description: A foundational Taoist text filled with stories, parables, and philosophical reflections. It encourages freedom from rigid thinking, acceptance of change, spontaneity, and alignment with nature. The teachings inspire readers to transcend limitations and embrace life's mysteries.

taoism.title: Wu Wei
taoism.description: The Taoist principle of effortless action. Rather than forcing outcomes, Wu Wei teaches acting in accordance with the natural flow of events. It promotes peace, effectiveness, and harmony by working with life's rhythms instead of against them.

taoism.title: Yin and Yang
taoism.description: The Taoist concept of complementary opposites. Yin and Yang represent balance in the universe, showing how seemingly opposing forces are interconnected and interdependent. Understanding this principle helps cultivate harmony in relationships, decisions, and daily life.

taoism.title: The Tao
taoism.description: The central concept of Taoism, often translated as 'The Way.' The Tao is the underlying natural order and source of all existence. It cannot be fully described in words but can be experienced through mindful living, simplicity, and alignment with nature.

buddhism.title: Dhammapada
buddhism.description: Verses on the path to enlightenment and ethical living.
